correctness.rationale: Exact equilibrium coordinate equation gives support iff incoming all-positive parent set. The half-density subsolution and monotone iteration give each and all Boolean fixed supports at one uniform large transmission scale. Descending hyperedge-core pruning and induction on deleted layers yield explicit \(C_m(1+t)^{m-1}\rho^t\) decay. Invariance and finite hyperedge assumptions were reconstructed and a 4096-graph standalone test passed. No finite test substitutes for the general proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Proposition 8 of the 2024 paper provides one spectral sufficient inequality for exponential healthy-state stability; this inequality can fail on acyclic AND-hyperedge networks at high rates despite guaranteed extinction. Proposition 9 instead requires a strictly positive vector and large-rate inequalities. Neither contains a classification of every fixed support; continuous-time 2023 Theorems 3/8 use irreducible or spectral hypotheses. The new statement uses a Boolean fixed-point equality, not a special choice satisfying their parameter inequalities.

value.rationale: Identifies, for arbitrary finite directed AND-hyperedge epidemiological networks, whether any endemic support can ever be sustained without numerical rate tuning; gives a polynomial-time structure-only peeling algorithm, all possible high-rate equilibrium supports, a uniform sufficient infection threshold and rigorous global extinction rate when no core remains. These are meaningful structural/epidemic intervention outputs, not a parameter substitution.
